subChunks.title: ROUND, ABS, and Arithmetic Expressions
subChunks.hookHtml: SQL lets you compute directly inside a query — rounding floats, taking absolute values, and building arithmetic expressions without fetching data into application code first.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Arithmetic in SELECT

SELECT xp, xp * 1.1 AS boosted_xp FROM apprentices;
SELECT xp, xp / 100.0 AS xp_hundreds FROM apprentices;

Integer division: 7 / 2 = 3 in most SQL engines. Use 7 / 2.0 = 3.5 or cast to float to avoid truncation.

ROUND

SELECT ROUND(3.14159, 2);     -- 3.14
SELECT ROUND(AVG(xp), 0) AS avg_xp FROM apprentices;

ABS — absolute value

SELECT ABS(-42);    -- 42
SELECT ABS(xp - 2000) AS distance FROM apprentices;

Other useful functions

  • CEIL(x) / CEILING(x) — round up
  • FLOOR(x) — round down
  • MOD(x, y) or x % y — remainder
  • POWER(x, n) — x to the nth power
  • SQRT(x) — square root

storyBeats.text: The treasury ledger surfaces — columns of raw floats and negative adjustments.

storyBeats.speaker: Cipher the Archivist
storyBeats.text: Compute in the query itself. Fetching raw numbers to the application just to multiply them is wasteful. ROUND, ABS, CEIL, FLOOR — the engine does arithmetic faster than your code will. Be cautious with integer division: 7 divided by 2 is 3, not 3.5, unless you cast one operand to a decimal.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
🪄 XP bonus

Return name and each apprentice's XP multiplied by 1.5, rounded to zero decimal places, aliased as bonus_xp.
subChunks.guidedPracticeStarterCode:
SELECT
  name,
  ROUND(xp * 1.5, 0) AS bonus_xp
FROM apprentices;

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain integer division in SQL and why dividing two integers might give a wrong answer. Give an example and the fix.

questions.explanation: ROUND(2.567, 1) rounds to one decimal place. 2.567 rounded to one decimal is 2.6 (the second decimal 6 >= 5, so the first decimal rounds up from 5 to 6).

questions.prompt: What does `SELECT 7 / 2` return in most SQL engines?
questions.explanation: Integer divided by integer performs integer division in most SQL engines, truncating the decimal. To get 3.5, write 7 / 2.0 or CAST(7 AS REAL) / 2.

questions.prompt: Which expression returns the remainder when xp is divided by 100?
questions.explanation: MOD(x, y) returns the remainder of x divided by y. xp % 100 is an equivalent shorthand in most engines.

questions.prompt: A developer computes `total_cost / units` where total_cost is INTEGER and units is INTEGER. Results are unexpectedly all zeros for small values. Why?
options: Integer division truncates toward zero — values less than units return 0
Division always returns zero when both operands are INTEGER
The column type must be FLOAT for any division
A WHERE clause is needed to exclude zero results
questions.answer: Integer division truncates toward zero — values less than units return 0
questions.explanation: If total_cost < units, the integer quotient is 0. Cast one operand: total_cost * 1.0 / units or CAST(total_cost AS REAL) / units to get fractional results.
